description: A weather forecast where each horizontal pill spans the day's low and high on a shared gradient scale.
overview: Uses `BarChart` with `layout="vertical"` and `barCategoryGap={7}`. `chartData` holds eight `{ day, low, high }` records mapped to add `range: [low, high]`; a `Bar` given a two-value array draws from the first value to the second. The `Bar` is fully rounded (`radius={99}`), has a track via `background={{ fill: "var(--control)", radius: 99 }}`, and is filled with a horizontal `linearGradient` from `var(--teal)` through `var(--yellow)` to `var(--orange)`. Two category `YAxis` elements show the day on the left and the high temperature on the right (`yAxisId="high"`), and the hidden `XAxis` is fixed to `domain={[8, 27]}`. `chartConfig` provides only a `label` for `range`.
usage: Replace the source records with your own `day`, `low` and `high` values and keep the `.map` that builds `range`. Set the `XAxis` `domain` to cover your coldest low and warmest high so every pill shares one scale. Edit the gradient stops to change the temperature colors, and adjust the tooltip `formatter`, which prints array values as a low-to-high string with degree signs.
notes: Because the gradient spans the whole plot width, each pill shows the slice of the scale its range covers. The gradient `id` comes from `React.useId()`. `accessibilityLayer` is set on `BarChart`, so the plot is focusable and arrow keys move between days.
